**Regrettably, insurance companies often attempt to exploit pre-existing medical conditions to limit their liability.** We foresaw their argument that some of the injuries might have been connected to her prior spine surgery.
However, in accordance with Texas law, the “Eggshell Doctrine” takes precedence. This principle dictates that the plaintiff should receive compensation for all injuries stemming from the accident, irrespective of any pre-existing conditions that may have exacerbated them.

Subsequently, the client underwent multiple laminectomies to address the damaged vertebrae.
When negotiations commenced with the insurer, they predictably contested that the accident’s force could not have warranted surgery. In response, Shane emphasized the well-documented new symptoms and underscored that even a moderate accident could worsen pre-existing injuries.
**In the end, the insurer was compelled to pay out $962,500.00.** What’s even more noteworthy, our reduced 29% case fee translated to a $70,000.00 savings for the client, as her claim was successfully settled without the need for litigation!

Speaking at a general level, personal injury claims need a few strong criteria to be successful. Ultimately, you’ll know for certain after talking to one of our lawyers. Here’s generally what we’ll look for:
### Did The Defendant Owe You A Duty Of Care?
You must have a legal or formal relationship or obligation with the defendant. For example, if you fall and get hurt at a neighbor’s house, they do owe you a duty of care and you might be able to hold them liable for your injuries. However, if you have a friend who’s a doctor and they give you advice while you meet for lunch, you can’t hold them legally responsible. That’s because they don’t owe you a duty of care in that situation. However, if you see them at their office and pay for their services, they do owe you a duty of care.
### Did The Defendant Breach That Duty Of Care?
In legal terms, this means the defendant must act with the watchfulness, attention, and prudence that a reasonable person would under the same circumstances. Failing to meet this duty means that you can possibly hold the person financially liable if their actions caused you injuries or damages.
### Did You Incur Damages As A Direct Result Of The Breach?
While you may experience an injury you believe happened as a direct result of someone else’s negligence, you must prove it. This can be quite difficult in some cases. For example, whiplash may not show up until several days after a car accident. Insurers will work hard to show that such an injury happened for some reason unrelated to the car accident.
### Did The Situation Happen Within The Past 2 Years?
In Texas, you have two years from the date of your accident to file your claim. Wait longer than that, and you can never again seek compensation for your injuries. At the same time, there are some exceptions to the “statute of limitations” as it is called. But these only apply to specific situations. So, you’re wise to pursue your claim as fast as possible.
### Did You Make Mistakes That Would Harm Your Case?
You don’t necessarily have to be perfect and completely blameless. But unfortunately, you can make mistakes that mitigate the compensation you receive, or even cause you to lose it all. For example, if you claim to be hurt by a slip and fall and then post pictures of yourself hiking on Facebook a few days later, you might lose your claim entirely. Or, if after a car accident you choose to ignore your doctor’s advice, the insurer can argue you had some blame for your injuries too. In that case, you could possibly miss out on some compensation you would otherwise get.
